newsitem.title: USA: Futures funds do well in currencies in May.
newsitem.headline: Futures funds do well in currencies in May.

text.p: For the second consecutive month, futures fund managers who trade the currency markets were the top performers for the month of May, according to fund monitor TASS Management Ltd.
Managed futures funds realised most of their gains during May from trading strategies linked to the U.S. dollar, Japanese yen and Deutschemark.
But futures funds also made good profits trading coffee and interest rate markets, TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
"Substantial volatility in global currencies presented managers with opportunities on both the long and short side of the market," Meaden said.
"Trades based on a strengthening of the U.S. dollar against major currencies seemed to be the most popular though."
The dollar saw a four and half year high against the yen in early May, and reached a three and half year high against the mark.
Overall performance by managed futures was only lackluster in May though, as in April, Meaden said.
The TASS Management monthly report follows the performance of 70 futures and currency managers, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Ltd is a London-based research company which monitors about 1,600 alternative investment managers with about $11 billion in assets under management globally.
The "alternative investment" universe includes hedge funds, CTAs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
